questions.question: How many peer operations do three debaters perform in a full mesh over three rounds?
questions.explanation: Each of three debaters sees the other two, giving six directed peer operations per round; three rounds therefore produce 18 operations.

questions.question: How many operations does the sparse-star topology use for the same three debaters and three rounds?
questions.explanation: The star has two hub-to-spoke and two spoke-to-hub operations per round, four total; over three rounds it uses 12.

questions.question: What answer do the scripted debaters converge on for the capital-of-Portugal question?
options: Lisbon, with convergence reported in round 1.
Porto, after three rounds of majority voting.
Madrid, because the hub's answer dominates.
No answer, because the debaters never share their first proposals.
questions.explanation: All three scripted drift functions settle on `Lisbon` in the first round, so the final majority answer is Lisbon and convergence is round 1.

questions.question: How does `run_debate` define `converged_round`?
options: It is always the configured final round.
It is the first round in which all current answers are identical.
It is the round with the most peer operations.
It is set only when a human approves the majority answer.
questions.explanation: After each round the implementation tests whether the current answer set has one value; the first all-equal round is stored as `converged_round`.

questions.question: What does a debater receive in its peer list during a full-mesh round?
options: Only the hub's answer, regardless of topology.
Its own answer twice, to stabilize self-consistency.
The current answers from every other debater, excluding itself.
A random sample that may include no other debater.
questions.explanation: `full_mesh_round` builds peers by filtering out the current debater's name, so each model sees the other two answers but not a duplicate of its own.

questions.question: How does the debate runtime choose the final answer after the last round?
options: It always returns the first debater's initial proposal.
It returns the answer from the hub, even in full mesh.
It concatenates every final answer for a human to choose.
It takes the most common value in the final answer mapping.
questions.explanation: The final result uses `Counter(prior.values()).most_common(1)[0][0]`, so it selects the majority value among the answers at the end of the configured rounds.
